question: Does the natural breadth-synchrony regime plane and its predeclared dispersion criterion survive equalizing temporal sampling depth across all admitted systems?

sampling.within_system: sample target_time_bins distinct source-native bins without replacement
sampling.across_systems: independent deterministic streams keyed by source_study_id|archipelago_id|system_id
sampling.partner_rule: retain the original partner columns; re-evaluate nonconstant-series eligibility after rarefaction
sampling.invalid_iteration_rule: an iteration is invalid if any admitted system has fewer than three nonconstant partner series after rarefaction

primary_sensitivity.name: phi_only
primary_sensitivity.breadth: retain full-data pooled effort-standardized Hill D1
primary_sensitivity.synchrony: recompute Loreau-de Mazancourt phi from the six-bin rarefaction
primary_sensitivity.rationale: isolates finite-time-bin sensitivity of the synchrony axis

secondary_sensitivity.name: joint_coordinate
secondary_sensitivity.breadth: recompute pooled Hill D1 from the same six selected bins
secondary_sensitivity.synchrony: recompute phi from the same six selected bins
secondary_sensitivity.rationale: tests the stronger common-window perturbation of both natural coordinates

prespecified_outputs: per-system rarefied phi median and 95% interval
leave-one-source-out dispersion-criterion pass fraction for every admitted source
interpretation_boundary: This is a sampling-depth sensitivity analysis of the already admitted natural regime plane. It does not reopen source admission, select systems by their coordinate values, change source-native partner identities, or create a natural analogue of synthetic k. Passing supports robustness to unequal temporal depth; failure narrows the natural claim to the observed sampling schedules.
